goal: Prove the same versioned birthday multi-agent scenario across at least two real providers without provider-specific success substitution.
required_outcome: A redacted exact-revision matrix of real provider runs, equivalent ACIP semantics, negative/provider-loss cases, and visible rejection of fixture, cached, receipt-only, or synthetic substitution.
task_boundary: Implement only the WP-18B provider-neutral harness, validator, proof matrix, traces, and failure cases over landed #5832, #5834, and #5836 contracts.
plan_summary: Verify #5832, #5834, and #5836; select two real independently configured providers; run the identical scenario and retain redacted ACIP traces; execute malformed, denied, interrupted, unavailable, loss, and substitution cases; validate source/provider truth and review exact head.
review_scope: Review the WP-18B real-provider harness, validator, matrix, redacted traces, negative artifacts, and exact proof paths for identical scenario/ACIP semantics, no substitution, credential safety, provider-loss isolation, and scope discipline.
operator_constraints: At least two independently configured real providers must pass
Provider unavailability is a non-pass and cannot trigger substitution
Never retain credentials, private prompts, or unredacted provider payloads
Release the preparation claim before handoff

authority_boundary: WP-18B owns provider comparison and no-substitution proof
Provider credentials and private payloads remain outside retained artifacts
initial_assumptions: #5834 supplies the integrated birthday review packet

deliverables: Provider-neutral matrix with at least two positive columns
Redacted ACIP traces and artifact digests
Malformed, denied, interrupted, unavailable, loss, and substitution proof
dependencies: Two approved real-provider credential sources available at execution time
non_goals: Changing ACIP or the birthday scenario
Publishing credentials, private prompts, or raw payloads

invariants: Every positive column is a real provider invocation
The scenario and ACIP operation contract are identical across providers
One provider failure does not terminate Runtime or unrelated agents
Retained artifacts are credential-free and redacted
risks: A provider may be unavailable or capability-incompatible
Trace redaction may remove evidence needed for comparison
stop_conditions: Fewer than two real compatible providers are available
No safe redacted trace can prove semantic equivalence
replan_triggers: Provider capability or API contract changes
A required platform lacks the provider tool

acceptance_criteria: AC-1: At least two real providers complete the identical versioned scenario through equivalent ACIP operations.
AC-2: Provider identity/capability truth and bounded semantic differences are retained without credentials or private payloads.
AC-3: Malformed, denied, interrupted, unavailable, provider-loss, and substitution cases have visible non-pass outcomes.
AC-4: One provider failure leaves Runtime and unrelated agents available, with macOS/Linux tooling posture recorded.
AC-5: Exact-head review has no unresolved actionable finding.

steps.action: Verify #5832, #5834, and #5836 exact contracts and select two real providers
Run the identical scenario and retain redacted ACIP traces
Execute provider failure and no-substitution negatives
Generate and validate the matrix, artifact index, redaction, and platform posture

validation_lanes.proof_role: Require two real-provider positive runs through the identical scenario and ACIP contract.
Reject malformed, denied, unavailable, lost, interrupted, cached, fixture, and receipt-only substitutions.
Validate credentials/redaction, matrix parity, Runtime isolation, and macOS/Linux tooling posture.

review_prompts: Do two real providers, rather than fixtures or cached output, complete the same scenario?
Are identity, authority, ordering, ACIP operations, and result semantics provider-neutral?
Do provider loss and substitution attempts fail visibly without collapsing Runtime?
Are all traces useful but credential-free and appropriately redacted?
